title: Sales & Marketing Case Study Study Plan

phases.title: Indian companies and organisations
phases.intro: Start here: 19 Indian cases on brands you already know, covering FMCG, rural selling, advertising, crisis recovery, pricing wars and new-age D2C brands. The IIM, ISB and ICMR versions are paid; the links below are free explainers.

phases.title: International companies
phases.intro: Next, 12 global cases that IIM and ISB marketing courses use to teach brand building, experience design, localisation, purpose marketing and digital growth. WARC links show award-winning campaign write-ups; a free WARC account unlocks some of them.

phases.title: Classic must-know cases
phases.intro: Finish with 10 classics: the Harvard decision cases most often used in IIM and ISB marketing courses, the failures every interviewer expects you to know, and the foundational ideas behind them. Harvard cases cost about $10-12 each on Harvard Business Publishing; the free student analyses below are enough to start.

cases.title: Amul: building India's biggest food brand as a farmers' co-op
cases.story: A Gujarat dairy co-operative took on multinationals with low prices, huge distribution and the Amul girl topical ads running since 1966.
cases.learn: Value-for-money positioning, mass-market distribution, mascot-led brand building.
cases.frameworks: 4Ps, STP, brand equity.

cases.title: Surf vs Nirma: Lalitaji and the detergent war
cases.story: Nirma sold detergent at a third of Surf's price and grabbed the mass market. HLL fought back with the Lalitaji ads (value over cheapness) and later launched Wheel as a low-price fighter brand.
cases.learn: Responding to a low-cost challenger, fighter brands, positioning on value rather than price.
cases.frameworks: Porter's generic strategies, market leader vs challenger, Ansoff.

cases.title: HUL Project Shakti: rural women as the last-mile sales force
cases.story: From 2001, HUL trained rural women (Shakti Ammas) as micro-entrepreneurs selling its products in small villages that its distributors could not reach profitably.
cases.learn: Rural distribution, inclusive business models, creating a new sales channel.
cases.frameworks: Bottom of the Pyramid, channel design, 4As of rural marketing (Availability, Affordability, Acceptability, Awareness).

cases.title: Fevicol: making glue a household name
cases.story: Pidilite turned a B2B adhesive for carpenters into an iconic consumer brand through decades of humorous ads on one idea: an unbreakable bond.
cases.learn: Consistent creative idea over decades, building brand in a low-interest category, influencing both end users and trade (carpenters).
cases.frameworks: Integrated marketing communication (IMC), positioning, push vs pull strategy.

cases.title: Cadbury India: the 2003 worm crisis
cases.story: Weeks before Diwali, worms were found in Dairy Milk bars in Maharashtra. Sales fell sharply. Cadbury responded with new tamper-proof packaging, a retailer education drive and ads with Amitabh Bachchan, and recovered within months.
cases.learn: Crisis communication, rebuilding trust, using a credible endorser.
cases.frameworks: Crisis management stages, brand trust, stakeholder mapping.

cases.title: Tanishq: winning trust in a market ruled by local jewellers
cases.story: Tanishq struggled after its 1994 launch. It turned around by installing Karatmeters so customers could test the purity of any gold, exposing impure local jewellery and positioning Tanishq on trust.
cases.learn: Using transparency as a brand weapon, organising a fragmented market, premium pricing justified by trust.
cases.frameworks: Positioning, consumer decision journey, brand turnaround.

cases.title: CavinKare Chik: the sachet revolution
cases.story: C.K. Ranganathan launched Chik shampoo in small sachets, ran a 'return empty sachets, get one free' scheme and later a 50-paise sachet, opening shampoo to rural buyers.
cases.learn: Small unit packs, price-point marketing, inducing trial.
cases.frameworks: Bottom of the Pyramid, 4As of rural marketing, sales promotion.

cases.title: ITC e-Choupal: internet kiosks for farmers
cases.story: ITC set up internet kiosks in villages so farmers could check prices and sell crops directly to ITC, bypassing middlemen. The same network later sold products into villages.
cases.learn: Building a two-way rural channel, technology in distribution, creating shared value.
cases.frameworks: Bottom of the Pyramid, value chain, channel design.

cases.title: Asian Paints: winning through distribution
cases.story: Asian Paints skipped bulk buyers and went straight to small retail dealers across India, using small packs, wide reach and later strong IT and demand forecasting. It became the market leader by distance.
cases.learn: Distribution as a competitive advantage, dealer management, demand forecasting.
cases.frameworks: Channel strategy, 4Ps (especially Place), Porter's Five Forces.

cases.title: Maggi: the 2015 ban and comeback
cases.story: In June 2015, Maggi was banned nationwide over lead and MSG allegations. Nestle destroyed tonnes of stock, fought in court, relaunched in November 2015 with a nostalgia-led campaign and regained most of its share.
cases.learn: Crisis response, relaunch strategy, emotional brand loyalty.
cases.frameworks: Crisis management, brand equity, relaunch marketing mix.

cases.title: Reliance Jio: free data and the telecom shake-up
cases.story: Jio launched in September 2016 with free calls and data, forcing rivals to slash prices. Several operators merged or exited. IIM Ahmedabad also has a companion case on Airtel's response.
cases.learn: Penetration pricing, disruption, how incumbents should respond.
cases.frameworks: Pricing strategy, Porter's Five Forces, game theory basics.

cases.title: Patanjali: Ayurveda, swadeshi and FMCG disruption
cases.story: Patanjali grew fast by selling low-priced Ayurvedic products with swadeshi messaging and Baba Ramdev as its face, forcing HUL, Colgate and others to launch natural ranges. Later growth slowed amid quality and regulatory issues.
cases.learn: Founder-led branding, cultural positioning, competitor response, risks of over- claiming.
cases.frameworks: Blue Ocean, positioning, SWOT.

cases.title: Tata Nano: why the world's cheapest car failed
cases.story: Launched in 2009 at about Rs 1 lakh, the Nano was marketed as the cheapest car. Buyers did not want to be seen in a 'cheap' car, early fire incidents hurt trust, and sales never reached targets.
cases.learn: Positioning failure, aspiration vs price, the gap between a great product and a wanted product.
cases.frameworks: STP, consumer behaviour, positioning.

cases.title: Royal Enfield: from near-shutdown to global icon
cases.story: In the early 2000s Eicher almost closed Royal Enfield. Siddhartha Lal kept it, fixed quality and leaned into heritage and leisure riding instead of mileage, creating a premium mid-size segment.
cases.learn: Brand turnaround, community building, premiumisation.
cases.frameworks: Positioning, brand revitalisation, customer communities.

cases.story: Zomato built a witty, meme-friendly brand voice and famous push notifications to drive repeat orders in a discount-heavy market against Swiggy.
cases.learn: Digital brand voice, retention marketing, social media as a growth channel.
cases.frameworks: Customer journey, AARRR funnel, brand personality.

cases.title: boAt: India's D2C audio brand
cases.story: boAt sold affordable, stylish earphones online through Amazon and Flipkart, used influencers, cricket and pop culture, and became India's top audio brand before growth flattened.
cases.learn: D2C playbook, influencer marketing, lifestyle positioning of a gadget.
cases.frameworks: STP, digital marketing funnel, product life cycle.

cases.title: Lenskart: omnichannel eyewear
cases.story: Lenskart started online, then realised eyewear needs eye tests and try-ons, so it built thousands of stores, home eye tests, virtual try-on and its own manufacturing.
cases.learn: Omnichannel retail, solving trust in an online category, vertical integration.
cases.frameworks: Customer journey, 7Ps, Porter's value chain.
cases.read: The D2C Pulse: Lenskart omnichannel strategy · ICMR: Lenskart in the Indian eyewear market · upGrowth: Lenskart GTM teardown
cases.tip: you see this model from the store floor every day. Add your own observations on walk-ins, eye tests and online-to-store handoffs to your notes; that turns this case into a portfolio piece.

cases.title: Mumbai Dabbawalas: near-perfect service at low cost
cases.story: About 5,000 dabbawalas deliver and return around 130,000 lunchboxes a day with very few errors, using a colour code, local trains and a flat co-operative structure. Harvard teaches it as 'The Dabbawala System'.
cases.learn: Service quality, process design, people over technology.
cases.frameworks: Service marketing 7Ps, service quality (SERVQUAL), operations basics.

cases.title: Byju's: when aggressive selling destroys a brand
cases.story: India's most valued startup grew on heavy advertising and high-pressure sales to parents, often on loans. Complaints, losses and governance problems led to collapse.
cases.learn: Ethics in sales, customer lifetime value vs short-term targets, brand trust.
cases.frameworks: Sales funnel, CLV, stakeholder analysis.

cases.title: Nike: 'Just Do It' (1988)
cases.story: In 1987 Nike was losing to Reebok and had laid off staff. Wieden+Kennedy's 'Just Do It' campaign shifted the brand from shoes to a mindset of personal achievement, and sales grew roughly tenfold in a decade.
cases.learn: Emotional branding, a simple durable tagline, athlete endorsements.
cases.frameworks: Brand positioning, brand equity, AIDA.

cases.title: Apple: 'Think Different' (1997)
cases.story: Apple was near bankruptcy when Steve Jobs returned. He cut the product line and launched 'Think Different', which sold Apple's values rather than specs and set up the iMac comeback.
cases.learn: Values-led branding, brand turnaround, focus.
cases.frameworks: Brand identity, positioning, Simon Sinek's Golden Circle (why, how, what).

cases.story: Starting in Australia, Coca-Cola replaced its logo with popular first names on bottles to reconnect with young people. It rolled out to 70+ countries and lifted consumption.
cases.learn: Personalisation, packaging as media, user-generated content.
cases.frameworks: Integrated campaigns, consumer engagement, earned media.

cases.title: Starbucks: the 'third place'
cases.story: Howard Schultz built Starbucks as a 'third place' between home and work, selling an experience rather than coffee. Rapid expansion diluted it, and in 2008 Schultz closed hundreds of stores to restore it.
cases.learn: Experience marketing, premium pricing, protecting brand experience while scaling.
cases.frameworks: Service 7Ps, experiential marketing, brand positioning.

cases.title: McDonald's India: glocalisation
cases.story: McDonald's entered India in 1996 without beef, created the McAloo Tikki and Maharaja Mac, separated veg and non-veg kitchens, and priced low to become an affordable family treat.
cases.learn: Glocalisation (global standards, local product), value pricing, cultural adaptation.
cases.frameworks: International marketing (standardise vs adapt), 4Ps, STP.

cases.title: IKEA India: entering a very different market
cases.story: IKEA studied Indian homes for years, then opened in Hyderabad in 2018 with India-specific products, a local menu, assembly help and lower prices for price- sensitive shoppers.
cases.learn: Market entry research, localisation beyond the product, pricing for a new market.
cases.frameworks: PESTEL, market entry strategy, Bowman's strategy clock.

cases.title: Dove: Campaign for Real Beauty (2004 onward)
cases.story: Research showed few women called themselves beautiful. Dove used real women in its ads and short films like 'Evolution' and 'Real Beauty Sketches', turning a soap into a self-esteem brand.
cases.learn: Insight-led advertising, purpose marketing, long-term brand platforms. Also study the criticism, as classes debate it.
cases.frameworks: Consumer insight, cause marketing, brand positioning.

cases.story: Red Bull barely advertises the drink. It sponsors and films extreme sports. In 2012 it live-streamed Felix Baumgartner's jump from the edge of space, watched by millions on YouTube.
cases.learn: Content marketing, owning a lifestyle, events as marketing.
cases.frameworks: Content strategy, brand associations, paid vs owned vs earned media.

cases.title: Old Spice: 'The Man Your Man Could Smell Like' (2010)
cases.story: P&G's Old Spice was seen as a grandfather's brand. A funny ad aimed at the women who buy body wash for men went viral, followed by 186 personalised YouTube replies, and it became the top men's body wash in the US.
cases.learn: Repositioning, targeting the buyer vs the user, real-time social marketing.
cases.frameworks: STP, buying roles (initiator, influencer, buyer, user), brand revitalisation.

cases.title: Domino's: the 'Pizza Turnaround' (2009)
cases.story: Domino's ranked last on taste. It filmed executives reading harsh customer reviews, admitted its pizza was bad, reinvented the recipe and later rebuilt itself as a tech-led delivery brand.
cases.learn: Radical honesty, listening to customers, product plus communication working together.
cases.frameworks: Brand turnaround, voice of the customer, pratfall effect.

cases.title: Netflix vs Blockbuster
cases.story: Netflix began as DVDs by mail with no late fees. Blockbuster reportedly declined to buy it for $50 million in 2000, depended on late fees, and went bankrupt in 2010 while Netflix moved to streaming.
cases.learn: Disruptive innovation, business model change, why market leaders miss threats.
cases.frameworks: Clayton Christensen's disruption theory, business model canvas, product life cycle.

cases.frameworks: STP, buying-decision influencers, diffusion of innovation.

cases.title: New Coke (1985)
cases.story: Losing share to Pepsi, Coca-Cola replaced its formula with a sweeter one that won blind taste tests. Loyal customers revolted, and the original returned as 'Coca- Cola Classic' after 79 days.
cases.learn: Emotional brand attachment, the limits of market research, listening to customers.
cases.frameworks: Brand equity, consumer behaviour, research design.

cases.title: Kodak: inventing the digital camera and still failing
cases.story: A Kodak engineer built the first digital camera in 1975. Kodak protected its high- margin film business, moved too slowly into digital, and filed for bankruptcy in 2012.
cases.learn: The innovator's dilemma, self-cannibalisation, defining your business by customer need.
cases.frameworks: Disruptive innovation, product life cycle, marketing myopia.

cases.story: Nokia led global mobile phones in the 2000s and even had touchscreen prototypes before the iPhone. It underrated software and app ecosystems, bet on Windows Phone, and sold its phone business in 2014.
cases.learn: Platform vs product competition, organisational fear and slow decisions, ecosystem thinking.
cases.frameworks: Disruption, SWOT, network effects.

cases.title: Marketing Myopia (Theodore Levitt, HBR 1960)
cases.story: Not a company case but the most famous marketing article. Railroads declined because they saw themselves in the railroad business, not the transport business. Companies fail when they focus on products instead of customer needs.
cases.learn: 'What business are you really in?', customer orientation vs product orientation. Reread Kodak, Nokia and Blockbuster through this lens.
cases.frameworks: Marketing concept vs selling concept.

cases.title: Harley-Davidson: the Harley Owners Group
cases.story: Near collapse in the early 1980s, Harley created the Harley Owners Group (HOG) in 1983. Owners rode together, attended rallies and shaped products, and HOG grew past a million members.
cases.learn: Brand communities, loyalty beyond discounts, identity-based brands. Compare with Royal Enfield (case 14).
cases.frameworks: Customer lifetime value, brand community, relationship marketing.
